title: Agent-first CLI: make aghist usable by AI agents (not just TUI users)
description:
**Goal**: Turn aghist from a TUI-with-some-flags into a CLI that AI agents can use programmatically — `aghist search`, `aghist export`, `aghist index`, `aghist mcp`, all with stable JSON output, deterministic ordering, and machine-readable errors.

**Why**: aghist already indexes 5 providers (Claude Code, Copilot, Gemini, Codex, OpenCode) with Tantivy. The TUI is the only consumer. Agents (and other tools) cannot search or filter from the CLI without entering the TUI.

**Reference research** (from session 2026-05-02):
- Closest competitors: CASS (`Dicklesworthstone/coding_agent_session_search`, 19 agents, SQLite + Tantivy + FastEmbed + RRF, MCP-friendly CLI), claude-history (Rust, Claude-only, indexes tool outputs).
- Agent-CLI design refs: beads `AGENTS.md`, `gt`, `gh`, `rg`, `ck`, `lnget` PR #14, googleworkspace/cli (runtime schema dump).
- MCP memory ecosystem: Mem0, mcp-memory-service, claude-context, ck (--serve mode).

**Scope** — sub-epics:
- ahist-? CLI primitives (search/json/exit-codes/schema)
- ahist-? Filters & citations (provider/since/role refs)
- ahist-? Index management (idempotent, observable)
- ahist-? Semantic search (FastEmbed, RRF, opt-in download)
- ahist-? MCP server (`aghist mcp` stdio)
- ahist-? Cross-machine sources (CASS-style remote indexes)
- ahist-? Decision/TODO extraction (research)

**Non-goals (this epic):** TUI overhaul, server-mode HTTP, write paths into agent histories.
close_reason: Agent-first CLI roadmap complete: y3o.1 CLI primitives, y3o.2 Filters & citations, y3o.3 Index management, y3o.4 Semantic search, y3o.5 MCP server, y3o.6 Cross-machine sources, y3o.7 Decision/TODO/threads. 24 commits across 24 leaves landed on main this session.

title: Unify JSON output envelope: {<plural>, meta} across list/search/sources/threads/todos/decisions
description:
Spike hq-cv-3ljdg cataloged 3 coexisting JSON-output wrapping conventions
across aghist subcommands. Implementation work to unify on a single envelope:

```
{ "<plural>": [...], "meta": { "count": N, "total": N, "next_cursor": null|"...", ... } }
```

Steps (from spike findings, see hq-cv-3ljdg notes for full analysis):

1. Fix `src/schema.rs:269-289` (search): declare wrapped `{hits, meta}`, not
   bare `array`. Runtime already emits the wrapped shape — pure docs fix.
2. Migrate `threads`/`todos`/`decisions` JSON output: move flat `count` under
   `meta.count`. Update schemas in `src/schema.rs:614-648`, `727-758`, `812-...`.
3. Migrate `sources`/`sources pull`/`sources list` (remote): hoist `index`,
   `cache_dir`, `config_path` under `meta`. Update schemas accordingly.
4. Standardise NDJSON: every stream subcommand ends with a trailing
   `{"meta":{...}}` line. Currently only `--list --ndjson` does this;
   `sources --ndjson` does not (`src/main.rs:2721-2727`).
5. Add a shared `agent_response_envelope` schema fragment in `src/schema.rs`
   and `$ref` it from each list-style schema.
6. Add an integration test asserting every list-style subcommand's JSON
   parses against the unified envelope shape.

Leaf commands (`show`, `index`, `health`, `sources add/remove`, `schema`)
stay flat — they aren't list responses. Document the distinction in
AGENTS.md alongside the error-envelope spec.

Backwards compatibility: aghist is v0.x, so a snap migration is acceptable.
If we want a softer landing, keep top-level `count` (deprecated alias) for
one minor cycle.

title: Provider slug serialization mismatch: kebab on input, snake in JSON output
description:
attached_molecule: ahist-wisp-jkyu
attached_formula: mol-polecat-work
attached_at: 2026-05-09T03:03:17Z
dispatched_by: unknown
formula_vars: base_branch=main

The CLI accepts `--provider claude-code` (kebab-case, per CLAUDE.md citation-ref contract) but JSON output (`--list`, search hits, `sources`, etc.) serializes the same field as `claude_code` (snake_case). Breaks naive round-tripping like `aghist --list --json | jq -r '.sessions[0].provider' | xargs aghist --provider` — fails because `claude_code` is rejected as a slug.

## Repro
```
target/release/aghist --provider claude-code --list --limit 1 --json | jq '.sessions[0].provider'
# prints "claude_code"
target/release/aghist --provider claude_code --list --limit 1
# error: unknown provider slug 'claude_code'. Valid: claude-code, ...
```

## Fix
Decide canonical slug shape and use it everywhere (CLAUDE.md says kebab; serde rename or impl Serialize on Provider). Probably want `#[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]` on the enum or matching custom Display/Serialize.

## Surfaces affected
- `aghist --list --json` sessions[].provider
- `aghist sources` provider field
- `aghist search --json` hit.provider
- `aghist show --format json`
- `aghist decisions --json`
- `aghist todos --json`
- `aghist threads --json`

title: Index management: idempotent CLI, observable, machine-readable health
Polecat clones inherit stale .beads/dolt-server.port from origin/main
description:
**Root cause** (verified 2026-05-02 via polecat furiosa autopsy):

bd's port resolution priority in worktrees:
1. Env var `BEADS_DOLT_PORT` — wins if set
2. `.beads/dolt-server.port` runtime file — but this is gitignored, so polecat worktrees never have it
3. `.beads/metadata.json` — bd documents this as "local, gitignored" and may not trust committed values
4. `.beads/config.yaml` `dolt.port: <N>` — should be honored but evidently isn't picked up by polecat clones

So polecat worktrees fall through to bd's compiled-in default (3307, which is HQ's port) and fail with `database "ahist" not found`.

**Inline fix shipped:** AGENTS.md now documents the `export BEADS_DOLT_PORT=$(cat /home/tien/projects/agent-history/.beads/dolt-server.port)` workaround so polecats find it in seconds.

**Real fix (deferred — likely upstream gt or bd):**
- Option A (gt): mol-polecat-work formula exports `BEADS_DOLT_PORT` from the project's live port file before invoking the polecat session.
- Option B (bd): honor `dolt.port` in committed `.beads/config.yaml` as the canonical default when no runtime port file exists.
- Option C (project): add a wrapper script (`.beads/hooks/...` or `~/gt/aghist/bin/bd`) that sets the env var on every bd invocation. Hacky.

Closing this issue once one of A/B is shipped upstream. For now the AGENTS.md workaround is sufficient.

title: Federated search clobbers source=local label when remote has overlapping content
description:
attached_molecule: ahist-wisp-khnt
attached_formula: mol-polecat-work
attached_at: 2026-05-09T11:06:48Z
attached_vars: ["base_branch=main"]
dispatched_by: unknown
formula_vars: base_branch=main

## Repro

```
target/release/aghist sources add fakebox --host localhost --path $HOME/.claude
AGHIST_RSYNC_BIN=/path/to/local-cp-wrapper target/release/aghist sources pull fakebox
target/release/aghist index   # 0 added, 1259 unchanged — content-hash dedupe working
target/release/aghist search 'polecat' --limit 20 --json | jq '[.hits[].source] | group_by(.) | map({k:.[0],v:length})'
# All 20 hits → source=fakebox; none labeled local, even though /home/tien/.claude has every session.
```

## Why this is wrong
`source` should reflect where the data is most cheaply readable. Local files exist on disk, no rsync round-trip needed; labelling them `fakebox` makes `aghist show <ref>` and follow-on lookups go through the remote-cache path unnecessarily, and breaks UX when the remote later disconnects.

## Likely fix
When the indexer sees two paths with identical content hash, prefer the local provider path's label over the remote-cache path. Or keep the source list in priority order and tie-break to the highest-priority one.

## Surfaces affected
- `aghist search --json` hit.source
- `aghist show <ref>` (may try to read from remote cache when local is available)
- Any consumer that reads `source` to decide where to deep-load content

## Repro env
- aghist 0.2.1
- y3o.6.3 federated search just landed (commit f40d0bc)

The three spike commands (y3o.7.{1,2,3}) were built by 3 polecats in parallel and ended up with different output shapes:

- `aghist decisions --json` → bare JSON array `[{...}, {...}]`
- `aghist todos --json` → wrapped `{count: N, todos: [...]}`
- `aghist threads --json` → wrapped `{count: N, threads: [...]}`

Pick one. The wrapped form is more useful (callers can branch on count, or extend with cursor/meta later). The CLI's other commands (`aghist --list --json`) use the wrapped `{meta: {...}, sessions: [...]}` form.

title: tests: copilot_v2/opencode_v2 discover_sessions fail on Linux due to Windows-style path parsing
description:
On Linux, two tests in tests/provider_format_diagnostic.rs fail because they expect a Windows-path normalization that doesn't apply on the host:

- copilot_v2_discover_sessions: assertion expected Some("myapp"), got Some("C:\\Users\\test\\myapp")
- opencode_v2_discover_sessions: assertion expected Some("myproject"), got Some("C:\\Users\\test\\myproject")

These were pre-existing on origin/main before ahist-y3o.1.1 (search subcommand) was implemented. The fixtures contain Windows paths (C:\\Users\\test\\...) and the providers are not extracting the basename when the path is Windows-style on a Linux host.

Likely fix: normalize/extract the basename in the copilot/opencode session discovery code, or split on both / and \\ when computing project_name.
